gsd.label: Geometric std. dev. of dry diameter

pairs.kelvin_off_transfer: Kelvin off in both + PyCHAM transfer coefficient in TOMAS-JAX
pairs.pycham_numerics: PyCHAM update step 10 s + rtol 1e-6 vs default

mismatches.what: Kelvin term. TOMAS-JAX (vbs-jax): Ke = exp(4 sigma MW_i / (R T rho_org Dp)) with sigma = 0.025 N/m, rho_org = 1200 kg/m3 and the condensing species' MW = 200. PyCHAM: Ke = exp(2 avMW sigma / (R T r rho_p)) with sigma = 72 mN/m (water), the particle's mass-weighted mean molar mass avMW (sulfate 96, organics 200, water 18) and the particle density.
mismatches.why: Hard-coded in both models (vbs-jax defaults; PyCHAM partit_var_prep.surfT = 72).
mismatches.effect: Nearly identical at t = 0 (Ke at 50 nm wet: 1.145 TOMAS-JAX vs 1.136 PyCHAM; PyCHAM's avMW of ~100 g/mol offsets its larger sigma). As SOA replaces sulfate PyCHAM's Ke grows (c* = 1, 12 h: 1.145 vs 1.195 at 50 nm, 1.070 vs 1.099 at 100 nm). Kelvin lowers c* = 100 SOA by 7.0 % (TOMAS-JAX) and 6.7 % (PyCHAM) at 12 h; the c* = 100 SOA difference of -0.26 % becomes +0.02 % with Kelvin off in both (patched PyCHAM copy with surfT = 0, vbs-jax sigma = 0).

mismatches.what: Gas-to-particle transfer coefficient. TOMAS-JAX: Fuller diffusivity with diffusion volume 120 (air 20.1), mean free path 2D/c, Fuchs-Sutugin in the Zaveri et al. (2014) form (0.283 coefficient). PyCHAM: Fuller with the diffusion volume from the SMILES (220.4, air 19.7), mean free path 3D/c, Fuchs-Sutugin in the Jacobson form (1.33 + 0.71/Kn).
mismatches.why: Each model's own formulation; PyCHAM has no input for the diffusion volume.
mismatches.effect: Diffusivity 7.18e-06 vs 5.56e-06 m2/s. Per particle TOMAS-JAX's coefficient is 1.32x PyCHAM's at 1 um, 1.47x at 54 nm and 1.50x at 1 nm, where it exceeds the gas-kinetic collision rate pi r^2 c N by 1.50x (vbs-jax pairs TOMAS's mean free path 2D/c with a Fuchs-Sutugin form defined for 3D/c). Condensation sink at t = 0: 0.00161 vs 0.00107 1/s (0.00111 with PyCHAM's formula on the TOMAS-JAX state). c* = 1 SOA +3.7 % (largest difference at 1-3 h) with Kelvin on; with Kelvin off in both it is +2.6 % and with PyCHAM's coefficient in TOMAS-JAX as well -1.1 %.

mismatches.what: Raoult term: mass fraction over the organic phase (TOMAS-JAX) vs mole fraction (PyCHAM). Made identical by giving POA and SURR the same SMILES (molar mass 200.23) and excluding sulfate (seed_diss = 0) and water (H2O_diss_wrtorg = 0) from PyCHAM's absorbing phase.
mismatches.effect: None by construction (TOMAS-JAX's 1e-4 absorbing floor adds 1e-4 x seed dry mass, < 0.03 % of the POA).

mismatches.what: Molar mass: 200 g/mol in TOMAS-JAX, 200.23 g/mol in PyCHAM (from the SMILES; PyCHAM has no molar-mass input).
mismatches.why: PyCHAM derives molar masses from SMILES.
mismatches.effect: Production and c* are converted with PyCHAM's molar mass, so the mass production and the mass-based c* are identical; the Kelvin exponent and mean molecular speed differ by 0.1 %.

mismatches.what: Particle water. TOMAS-JAX: ezwatereqm ammonium-bisulfate ratio, 0.3470 kg water per kg SO4 (x1.2 for NH4HSO4) and 0.2891 per kg of organics (A9), no Kelvin term. PyCHAM: water partitions with Raoult, with per-component dissociation constants w.r.t. water (core 1.8516, POA/SURR 3.2163) that give TOMAS-JAX's water mass when Kelvin = 1, plus its own Kelvin term (72 mN/m).
mismatches.why: PyCHAM has no fixed hygroscopic-growth input; its water always feels Kelvin.
mismatches.effect: c* = 1: total particle water -13.2 % in PyCHAM at t = 0 (0.179 vs 0.206 ug/m3) and -9.3 % at 12 h (1.481 vs 1.633); in the most populated bin at t = 0 (the 50 nm seed mode, where PyCHAM's Kelvin term on water is large) water/dry is 0.256 vs 0.330 (-22.4 %). c* = 100: TOMAS-JAX's wet number-mean diameter is +2.6 % vs PyCHAM at 12 h. With Kelvin off in both, TOMAS-JAX water is +0.20 % vs PyCHAM (c* = 1, 12 h). Water does not absorb organics in either model, so it acts only through size.

mismatches.what: Density. TOMAS-JAX: Tang (1997) H2SO4-solution density of the wet particle with organics counted as sulfate (1.682 g/cm3 for the initial wet seed). PyCHAM: volume-additive mixture with water fixed at 1.0 g/cm3 (a dens_Comp entry for H2O is ignored). The dry components (core, POA, SURR) get an effective 2.170 g/cm3, chosen so that m_dry/rho_d + m_w/1.0 equals TOMAS-JAX's Tang wet volume at t = 0 (water/dry 0.3296).
mismatches.effect: Identical wet volume at t = 0. Later the composition changes: applying the two density rules to the TOMAS-JAX particles at 12 h (c* = 1) gives wet densities that differ by up to 0.6 % (0.2 % in diameter).

mismatches.what: Size structure. TOMAS-JAX: two-moment sectional on 40 fixed mass-doubling bins with MNFIX. PyCHAM: moving-centre on the same bins (manual bounds in wet radius), same number per bin at t = 0, bins with < 1e-06 cm-3 left empty (1.2e-06 cm-3 in total).
mismatches.effect: Identical initial number and dry mass per bin (checked to 1e-9).

mismatches.what: Growth across bins. TOMAS-JAX's SOA step moves particles between its fixed bins only through MNFIX (vbs-jax redistribute hook): when a bin's mean dry mass leaves the bin, part of the population stays at the bin's geometric-mean mass and the rest jumps to 1/1.1 of the next bin's upper edge. PyCHAM's moving-centre bins keep each population's exact size.
mismatches.why: Size-structure numerics of each model (two-moment fixed sectional vs moving-centre).
mismatches.effect: Numerical spreading of the TOMAS-JAX distribution when particles grow over several bins (c* = 1: number-mean dry diameter -12.6 % vs PyCHAM at 12 h with 40 bins, +0.73 % with 160 bins in both; PyCHAM itself changes by -0.01 % from 40 to 160 bins). Mass is unaffected.

mismatches.what: Time stepping. TOMAS-JAX: source added every 60 s micro-step, then vbs-jax adaptive analytic sub-steps (operator split), Kelvin/CS frozen per sub-step. PyCHAM: continuous influx inside the BDF solve (rtol 1e-4), partitioning coefficients and Kelvin refreshed every 60 s update step.
mismatches.effect: TOMAS-JAX micro-step 10 s vs 60 s: SOA within 0.8 % after 1 h; PyCHAM update step 10 s and rtol 1e-6 vs default: SOA within 0.03 % after 1 h.

mismatches.what: c* at the run temperature: TOMAS-JAX's c* is defined at 298.0 K (vbs-jax T_REF) and corrected to 298.15 K with dHvap = 131 - 11 log10 c* kJ/mol (c* = 1 -> 1.0270). PyCHAM gets volP from this corrected c* (1.2714e-05 Pa for c* = 1; volP is constant in T).
mismatches.why: PyCHAM's volP is a fixed pressure.

mismatches.what: Chemistry. PyCHAM needs at least one reaction, so it gets the dummy `<1> SURR = SURR : 0.0`; TOMAS-JAX has chemistry off. The surrogate is a continuous influx (Cinfl = 1.6970e-05 ppb/s with TOMAS-JAX's air number density).
